manifest.name: @dsh-plugin/water-reminder
manifest.description: Hydration and posture reminder for DeepSeek Harness: two independent randomized tracks (drink water every 40-60 min, stand up / move / look into the distance every 45-70 min) delivered as a native OS notification, an in-conversation agent reminder, a sidebar countdown panel, and an embedded hydration-coach skill
manifest.author: light

bundle.text:
# water-reminder bundle patch.
#
# Mounting this package inserts one plugin row. The defaults below are complete
# on purpose: a user patch replaces the whole entry config, so restate every
# field you want to keep when overriding one of them.
#
# Installing the bundle appends the package to the profile's
# `dsh.profile.bundles`, and this layer mounts the row:
#
#   dsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/water_reminder
#
# If the profile's own cordis.patch.yml already has a `water-reminder` row,
# delete it first: two live entries would each start a reminder timer and each
# register the `/water/api` prefix route, and the duplicate route makes the
# plugin fail to boot.
- insert:
    - id: water-reminder
      name: '@dsh-plugin/water-reminder'
      config:
        # Whether the reminder loop runs at start-up. The panel and the
        # `water_control` tool can toggle it at runtime without touching this.
        enabled: true
        # The random interval window, in minutes. Every reminder draws a fresh
        # value from this band — the irregularity is the point, since a fixed
        # metronome is what people learn to dismiss.
        intervalMinMinutes: 40
        intervalMaxMinutes: 60
        # Daily intake goal and the volume recorded for one "cup".
        dailyGoalMl: 2000
        cupMl: 250
        # How long `water_snooze` defers when no explicit delay is given.
        snoozeMinutes: 5
        # Hold reminders back inside this local-time window; the pending
        # reminder is pushed to the window's end instead of firing.
        quietHours:
          enabled: false
          from: '22:00'
          to: '08:00'
        # The movement / eye-break track: an independent loop that nudges the
        # user to stand up, move around, or look into the distance. It keeps
        # its own band, so the two cadences can be tuned separately.
        posture:
          enabled: true
          intervalMinMinutes: 45
          intervalMaxMinutes: 70
          # Which nudges the track may deliver. At least one stays on.
          stand: true
          move: true
          distance: true
        # Delivery channels. `os` needs a subprocess provider (osascript on
        # macOS, a WinRT toast on Windows, notify-send on Linux); `agent`
        # injects one line into every live root session.
        notify:
          os: true
          agent: true
          sound: true
        # Expose a short system-prompt section describing the reminder loop.
        promptSection: true
        # Register the embedded `hydration-coach` skill through ctx.skills, so
        # the model gets the workflow with no filesystem skill root.
        skill: true
        # State file location. Defaults to $DSH_HOME/water-reminder.json, which
        # keeps the intake log out of the repository.
        # stateFile: /absolute/path/water-reminder.json

readme.text:
A **hydration and posture reminder** plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness).

People forget to drink while they are deep in work — and just as often forget to stand up. While a session is live this plugin runs **two independent reminder tracks**, and delivers each reminder through three independent channels — missing one still leaves two:

| Track | What it nudges about | Default rhythm |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 💧 Hydration | Today's intake and how much is left | every **40–60 minutes, drawn at random** |
| 🚶 Movement | Standing up and stretching, moving around, looking into the distance (eye strain) | every **45–70 minutes, drawn at random** |

| Channel | How it lands | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 🖥️ OS notification | `osascript` on macOS, a WinRT toast on Windows, `notify-send` on Linux | `ctx.subprocess` (part of dsh-base) |
| 💬 In-conversation nudge | a plugin message injected into every live root session, so the assistant says one line | the `agents` service |
| 🔔 Browser notification | the sidebar panel watches `reminderSeq` and the tab raises its own notification | page open + user permission |

The two tracks keep their own rhythm, their own on/off switch, and their own state — **pausing one leaves the other running**. Plus a **sidebar countdown panel**, a **settings page**, and an embedded `hydration-coach` **skill**.

The irregularity is the point. A perfectly regular timer is what teaches people to ignore it — which is why "drink water on the hour" apps get switched off. Redrawing the interval from the band on every reminder keeps the rhythm unpredictable, which is what makes it work.

The movement track works the same way, and it also draws the *reminder content*: stand up and stretch, move around, or look into the distance. Random, so the nudge does not decay into one repeated sentence.
```sh

readme.section: from a local checkout (writes the profile's package.json and dsh.profile.bundles)
readme.text: dsh plugin --profile web add link:/path/to/water_reminder

pnpm pack && dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-plugin-water-reminder-$(node -p "require('./package.json').version").tgz
```

Then reload the harness. On DeepSeek Harness ≥ 0.2.1-alpha.3 with hot reload enabled, code updates to this plugin apply without a restart; a fresh install (and toggling the load-time switches `promptSection` / `skill`) still needs one — restart `dsh web`. Never keep two `water-reminder` rows in one profile — each would start its own timer and register the `/water/api` prefix route, and the duplicate route makes the whole plugin tree fail to boot.
> Recreating a profile with `dsh … --from-default-profile` **replaces** that profile, including its plugins — re-add the plugin afterwards.

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `water_status` | Today's intake, remaining, cups, goal streak, current band, quiet hours, next reminder, 7-day series |
| `water_log` | Record a cup (defaults to the configured cup size; accepts `milliliters` and `note`). Append-only, never deduplicated |
| `water_snooze` | Defer the next reminder; defaults to 5 minutes |
| `water_control` | `start` / `stop` / `set-band` / `set-goal` / `remind-now` / `reset` |

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `posture_status` | Breaks taken today, next break reminder, current band, which nudges are enabled, last break |
| `posture_log` | Record one break (`action` is `stand` / `move` / `distance`; accepts `note`) |
| `posture_control` | `start` / `stop` / `set-band` / `remind-now` / `reset` |
`water_control` and `posture_control` write **runtime overrides** into the state file rather than editing the profile config; `reset` drops those overrides and falls back to configuration.
In the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (defaults ship in the plugin's own `cordis.patch.yml`):

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Whether the hydration loop runs at start-up |
| `intervalMinMinutes` | number | `40` | Lower bound of the hydration interval, in minutes |
| `intervalMaxMinutes` | number | `60` | Upper bound of the hydration interval, in minutes |
| `dailyGoalMl` | number | `2000` | Daily intake goal |
| `cupMl` | number | `250` | Milliliters recorded for one "cup" |
| `snoozeMinutes` | number | `5` | Default deferral for `water_snooze` |
| `quietHours.enabled` | boolean | `false` | Hold reminders inside a local-time window |
| `quietHours.from` / `.to` | string | `22:00` / `08:00` | The window (may wrap past midnight); a draw inside it resumes at the window's end |
| `posture.enabled` | boolean | `true` | Whether the movement loop runs at start-up |
| `posture.intervalMinMinutes` | number | `45` | Lower bound of the movement interval, in minutes |
| `posture.intervalMaxMinutes` | number | `70` | Upper bound of the movement interval, in minutes |
| `posture.stand` | boolean | `true` | May deliver the "stand up and stretch" nudge |
| `posture.move` | boolean | `true` | May deliver the "move around" nudge

The band is clamped to `[5, 720]` minutes (`[10, 360]` for the movement track), the goal to `[200, 20000]` ml, and the cup to `[50, 2000]` ml. **A user patch replaces the whole entry config**, so restate every field you want to keep when overriding one.

At least one movement nudge always survives: if all three are switched off, the track falls back to "stand up" rather than becoming a silent timer.

- **Sidebar footer 💧 button** — carries the live countdown to the next hydration reminder (shows "Paused" while off, ✅ once the goal is met). The panel has today's progress bar, cups/streak/band, next reminder, **next movement reminder with today's break count**, a 7-day bar chart, `+250ml` logging, snooze, remind-now, pause/resume, a **"take a break" logger**, and a control to grant browser-notification permission.
- **Settings page** — the full rhythm/goal/quiet-hours/channels form plus a **"Movement and eye breaks" section** (switch, band, and one toggle per nudge). Writes land in `$DSH_HOME/settings.yaml` and hot-reload; changing a band or quiet hours rearms the timer immediately.
The two switches marked "(restart)" (`promptSection`, `skill`) are read at load time and need a Harness reload.

The same instructions ship two ways:

1. **Runtime registration** — at mount the plugin calls `ctx.skills.register()`, so the model sees `hydration-coach` in its skill catalog with no filesystem skill root at all.
2. **On disk** — `skills/hydration-coach/SKILL.md`, for deployments that prefer a filesystem skill root (`~/.dsh/skills`, `~/.agents/skills`, a project `.dsh/skills`).

`skill.js` is the single source of truth and `npm test` asserts the checked-in SKILL.md matches the embedded body byte for byte, so the two delivery paths cannot drift. Run `npm run skill` after editing the body.

The skill covers which tool to call when, how to react to both reminder kinds (`[water-reminder]` and `[posture-reminder]`) — one short line, no health lecture, never derail the current task — logging rules, how to retune each track's rhythm, estimating a personal goal from body weight (30 ml × kg), and tone/safety boundaries (no medical claims).

- **The state file owns the state.** Timers, next due times, the intake log, and the break log live in `$DSH_HOME/water-reminder.json`, written through a temp file plus rename so a crash cannot truncate it. Both tracks share one file (hydration at the top level, movement under `posture`), so an existing state file keeps working.
- **No backlog after a restart.** A stale `nextDueAt` draws a fresh interval instead of firing the missed reminders at once.
- **Quiet hours** push a draw inside the window to the window's end rather than redrawing, so the behaviour stays predictable. Both tracks share that window.
- **A manual reminder leaves the rhythm alone.** `remind-now` delivers once without resetting the pending reminder.
- **Disposal drains.** Unloading the plugin waits for an already-queued state write, so a cup logged at the last moment is not lost.
- **The timers are `unref()`ed**, so neither reminder loop keeps the process alive.

- **Reminders only exist while Harness is alive.** There is no email, SMS, or push channel. With the process down, only the OS notification path exists — and only while it is up.
- **The Windows toast needs WinRT**, invoked as `powershell -EncodedCommand` (UTF-16LE base64) so quoting and CJK text are safe. If PowerShell is restricted by policy the reminder degrades to a log line, while the other two channels still fire.
- **Browser notifications need a user gesture** to request permission; the 🔔 control in the panel is that gesture.
- **The 7-day series is panel-only.** `water_status` returns a compact one-line text form instead, which keeps the tool's output schema free of nested arrays.
- **The movement track counts breaks, not duration.** `posture_log` records "you took a break", not how long it lasted or how many rounds. Finer tracking needs its own tool.

The plugin has **zero runtime dependencies** — `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools`, `dsh-llm`, `schemastery` and
friends are peer dependencies that the Harness supplies at runtime.

The versions this plugin develops against are published to npm, but **not under npm's `latest`
tag**: npm's `latest` for `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` is still the placeholder `0.0.1-rc.1`, while this
plugin targets `0.2.2-rc.1` (reached through the `next` dist-tag). Install the exact versions
from `devDependencies` rather than letting a resolver follow `latest`:

```sh
pnpm install        # resolves the pinned devDependencies
npm test            # 91 pass / 0 skip, including the real cordis composition tests
```

> **Companion versions.** `0.2.2-rc.1` is paired with `@deepseek-ai/cordis` `4.1.0` and
> `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` `3.19.0` (both real releases on their own `latest` channel now).
> The `rc.1` release has no dedicated `dsh-0-2-2-*` dist-tag —
> the exact version strings in `devDependencies` are the only source of truth.

> **Tool executor.** Since `0.2.2-alpha.2` the tool registry no longer owns the model-facing tool
> descriptions: assembling the system prompt asks the registry for its executor and throws
> `TOOL_EXECUTOR_UNAVAILABLE` when the composition has none. A real deployment gets one from
> `@deepseek-ai/dsh-base`; any composition you build by hand has to mount
> `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-executor-native` after the registry, which is what
> `test/integration.test.js` does.

If you prefer to reuse the packages from an existing local Harness profile (fastest, offline):

```sh
mkdir -p node_modules/@deepseek-ai
for p in cordis cosmokit dsh-llm dsh-tools dsh-settings dsh-skill dsh-system-prompt dsh-tool-executor-native schemastery; do
  ln -sfn "$HOME/.dsh/profiles/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/$p" "node_modules/@deepseek-ai/$p"
done

You can also build the Harness from source and link this plugin the way it documents:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness
```

The settings page and config hot reload require a Harness >= `0.1.2-alpha.3` host; on older hosts the
plugin still runs on its boot-time config.

> **Message source kind.** Since dsh `0.2` the harness has no shared catch-all `kind: 'plugin'`
> message source — each producer declares its own kind. This plugin injects under
> `'water-reminder'`, declared in [`types/dsh-llm.d.ts`](types/dsh-llm.d.ts). A pure-JavaScript
> plugin cannot use an inline `declare module` (that is TypeScript syntax, which Node rejects at parse
> time), so the type-level merge lives in that separate file.

Use the pinned install or the profile symlinks for the full suite
(`hydration.js` / `posture.js` / `notify.js`).

```sh
npm test              # 91 tests with dependencies; fewer pass + 2 skip without
npm run skill         # regenerate SKILL.md from skill.js
npm run skill:check   # verify SKILL.md is in sync
```

| File | Coverage | Needs Harness |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `test/hydration.test.js` | Pure logic: band normalization, random-draw bounds, quiet hours across midnight, streaks, summary, config completion | no |
| `test/posture.test.js` | Pure logic: movement-track action set, band clamping, state normalization, break log and counts | no |
| `test/notify.test.js` | Exact per-platform `argv`, AppleScript/XML escaping, PowerShell encode round-trip | no |
| `test/skill.test.js` | Embedded skill identical to the on-disk `SKILL.md` byte for byte, spec-compliant name, tool names complete | no |
| `test/client-structure.test.js` | Browser half: theme token names, hard-coded fills, locale key parity | no |
| `test/plugin.test.js` | Tool behavior against a minimal fake context, asserting every result matches its own declared `output.schema` | **yes** |
| `test/integration.test.js` | Mounted on a **real** `Context` with the real `tools`/`skills`/`systemPrompt` services: dependency resolution, skill discoverability, clean disposal, and no disk writes during teardown | **yes** |

When the packages are missing, the `plugin` and `integration` files **skip with a printed reason** instead of
turning the suite red.
